Only the two established Knights are in view at this landing; this establishes no omniscient absence of Knights elsewhere. Announced Stealth Standard52 against escort Perception Standard45 and corporal Perception Hard30, distracted by the knot. Engine rolls Halla50 success, escort73 failure, corporal30 success; Halla's higher successful roll wins the contest, so he closes unnoticed. Announced Intimidation Easy84 for the unexpected close approach against corporal Willpower Standard50. Halla speaks the player's line verbatim: "haven’t you bastards got anything better to do". Opposed engine rolls Halla30 success, corporal34 success, winner corporal. He turns, keeping one hand on the mooring rope and putting the other on his sword hilt. "We've got orders. Step back." His escort turns her shield toward Halla. Knot tied; swords sheathed; no attack, throw or seizure. Halla now beside Rusk's mooring rather than his first post. No Luck spent, no fumble or improvement. Prompt: "What do you do?".

narrative: The provisioning escort's committed interrupting sword attack rolled74 against65 and failed. narrative: Halla chooses Trip and Disarm from his critical battleaxe parry6. The escort resists Trip with Brawn63/55 failure and Disarm with Dragon Knight89/65 failure. She falls prone and her longsword lands three feet away on the dry quay. Halla's already-paid attack resumes: Battleaxe70/81 success beats corporal Round shield22/65 success with no special effects. summary: TABLE2c Shoals drawn-weapons incident: public ordinary with two prior reports, awareness bar45. d10080 fails; Tat resistance-awareness clock remains2/6. No named report, retaliation, bounty, route closure or invitation generated.
Halla steps back and drives both Knights away with Intimidation81 over Willpower39; encounter ends without injury.
narrative: Halla steps back with both axes and says, 'Fuck off now. Both of you. No point in anyone dying here.' Intimidation Easy81/84 success beats the corporal's Willpower39/50 success. The corporal tells the escort, 'Get your sword. We're leaving.' She recovers her longsword, and both Dragon Knights withdraw from the landing. Halla, Rusk and both crews remain uninjured. Bera's boats, grain, lines and crews remain secure. Halla has two Luck and the morning job remains underway.

summary: Halla covers the Knights' approach and orders the boats prepared for a rapid departure.
narrative: After the Dragon Knights withdraw, Halla takes a quayside guard position with a clear line of sight along their approach and across both grain boats. He tells the boatmen to prepare to leave quickly if needed. The crews keep unloading while readying the mooring lines and deck for rapid departure. No roll is required and no cargo is lost.

summary: Bera's two boats cast off rapidly from the Shoals with crews and cargo secure.
narrative: At Halla's direction the boatmen cast off from the Shoals immediately. Both boats leave together with Bera's crews and remaining cargo secure. Halla boards the lead boat with battleaxe and handaxe still drawn, keeping a clear lookout behind and between the boats. Rusk remains with the second boat. The morning guard job continues and remains unpaid.

summary: Halla stows both axes after leaving the Shoals confrontation.
narrative: Once the boats are clear of the Shoals confrontation, Halla secures his battleaxe and returns the handaxe to his belt. His armour and helm remain worn, his dagger remains sheathed, and both hands are free. No roll or resource expenditure is required.

summary: Temerach wins the open archery decisively and preserves her public standing instead of accusing Hanzo.
narrative: At the d0/day open archery at the Long Butts, Temerach's Knight of the Lake bow style Hard81 rolls2 critical against the household archer's Hard60 roll52 success, so Temerach wins the wreath decisively. Her passion to see Hanzo answer rolls60/75 success against her Willpower9/100 critical; restraint wins. She accepts the prize with the required public words and makes no accusation. Hanzo witnesses the result. Halla is absent on Bera's guard job and does not know this yet.

summary: Bera's morning delivery run finishes safely; Halla and Rusk receive two gold each.
narrative: By d0/day Bera's two boats complete the remaining morning deliveries and return to her water-stair with both crews and cargo secure. Bera pays Halla and Rusk the agreed two gold each and says, 'Two each. Good work.' Halla's purse rises from five to seven gold; his debt to Crowbill remains fourteen gold. Halla remains uninjured with two Luck, battleaxe secured and handaxe at his belt.

summary: Halla reaches the Long Butts after Bera's morning guard run in time to witness the final arrow, the score flag and Temerach Nebulo receiving the open-archery wreath.
narrative: Halla arrives at the Long Butts as the final arrow is loosed. The target marshal's flag confirms Temerach Nebulo as the decisive winner over the remaining household archer. She accepts the wreath before the Governor's box while Baron Hanzo is present. Halla witnesses the public result; no conversation occurs.

summary: Halla watches Baron Hanzo and searches the Long Butts for Commander Vask; Perception18/65 succeeds. Hanzo remains at the Governor's rail through Temerach's award, while Vask is absent from the visible escort and shooting ground.

Halla scans the dispersing archery crowd for familiar faces and pickpockets. His Perception98/65 fails against Pell Nettles' Stealth21/58 success; no additional acquaintance stands out, and Pell reaches Halla's purse cord unseen. The cord is taut in Pell's hand, but the pouch has not yet been taken.

Halla grabs for the crowd thief's wrist and attempts a takedown. Halla Unarmed16/74 succeeds, but Pell Nettles Evade41/48 is the stronger success. Pell twists free and abandons the purse; Halla retains all seven gold, nobody is injured, and Pell flees into the dispersing crowd.

Halla watches for a second thief after Pell escapes. Halla Perception68/65 fails against Joss Fen Stealth35/55 success. Halla identifies no accomplice; Joss leaves cleanly without touching Halla or taking property. Halla keeps all seven gold, while Pell and Hanzo disappear into the dispersing crowd.
Halla crosses the closing shooting ground and offers Temerach Nebulo his respects for winning the open archery. Temerach accepts the courtesy and asks, 'You're entered tomorrow?'
Halla confirms to Temerach, 'Aye. I am,' when asked whether he is entered tomorrow. Temerach notes that Halla watched Hanzo leave and asks why.
narrative: At the Long Butts after the archery award, Halla confirms his entry in tomorrow's single combat. Temerach packs her bowstring, looks toward the west gate Hanzo used, and asks Halla why he watched Hanzo leave.

summary: Halla tells Temerach that regular guard work for worried merchants has put him into repeated confrontations with Dragon Knights. Temerach calls it mercenary work and warns him that the marshals are watchful after the purse-thief scuffle. Halla praises her shooting and says he hopes to see her on the sands tomorrow; she answers, 'And you as well.' Halla checks his purse and kit: all seven gold and every carried item remain secure.
Halla pays Crowbill six gold in cash at the waterside office. Halla's purse falls from seven gold to one, and Crowbill records the debt falling from fourteen gold to eight.

After recording Halla's six-gold payment and the new eight-gold balance, Crowbill tells Halla: 'Hanzo takes his locket off at night; it lies beside his bed in the DragonBarge's aft cabin, and Vask sleeps across the door.'

The locket disclosure prepared after Halla's payment was retracted before delivery because Halla interrupted to ask about Dragon Knight activity. Payment remains live: Halla has1GP and owes8GP. Crowbill has not yet mentioned the locket or Nus.

Halla tells Crowbill that Thorne is matching worried merchants and boat owners with paid guards, and that the work is growing as Dragon Knights reach for barges and cargo. Crowbill answers, 'It is. Cargo disappears, crews refuse runs, and money that once bought transport now buys guards through Thorne.' He asks, 'Does Thorne know you're telling me?'

Halla tells Crowbill, "No. I'm assuming that in this matter, your interests align." Crowbill confirms, reveals Hanzo's nightly locket routine, and offers Halla guard work: "I need a guard, not a thief. Tomorrow night after your bout, get a boy onto the DragonBarge and back alive with the locket, and the eight gold left on this page disappears." Halla has not accepted or refused.
narrative: Crowbill confirms that his interests align with Halla's concern about the Dragon Knights. He reports that Hanzo removes the locket at night and leaves it beside his bed in the DragonBarge's aft cabin while Vask sleeps across the door. Crowbill does not ask Halla to steal it. He offers to clear Halla's remaining eight-gold debt if, tomorrow night after Halla's bout, Halla protects an unnamed boy's infiltration and gets him back alive with the locket. The boy remains in the adjoining room and has heard the exchange. Halla has not answered.

summary: Halla firmly refuses Crowbill's DragonBarge contract as suicidal. Crowbill accepts the refusal without pressure, withdraws the offer, and confirms Halla's account remains at eight gold.
narrative: Halla says, "Are you mad? The DragonBarge? That would be suicide." Crowbill's crow-marked hand settles flat over the account book. "Likely. Desperation made me ask; sense made you refuse. The barge is off the table. Your account stands at eight." He closes the ledger. "Anything else?"

summary: OOC player proposal: Randall might later impersonate Santo as the cover story used to draw Hanzo from the DragonBarge. This is a possible route only. Neither Halla nor Crowbill currently knows Randall, Santo, or their resemblance, and no in-world plan or knowledge is established.

Halla offers to cover the unnamed boy's escape from shore if Crowbill can first draw Hanzo and Vask away from the DragonBarge. Crowbill makes a revised eight-gold offer in which Halla never boards; Halla has not accepted.
narrative: Halla tells Crowbill he is interested in hurting the Baron by other means. If Crowbill can draw Hanzo off the DragonBarge with a convincing cover story, Halla offers to cover the boy's escape if pursuit follows. Crowbill opens the ledger one finger's width. "Hanzo can be drawn ashore. Vask is the difficulty. If I can move them both, you wait on the quay, cover the boy's retreat, and never set foot on the barge. Eight gold if he reaches me alive with the locket." He leaves the page open. "That one?"

summary: Halla accepts Crowbill's DragonBarge contract, saying, 'This sounds dangerous- Ok, if it means we get clear of our obligation to you. You're on.' Crowbill confirms that the remaining eight-gold debt clears when Halla and Nus both return alive with Hanzo's locket, then calls Nus into the office.

Halla asks for more manpower on the quay. Crowbill conditionally promises two disguised porters and an oarsman in a waiting skiff, with Halla holding the water-stair. The revised job remains unaccepted.
narrative: Halla says, "We'll need more than one of your men on the quay. You have anyone else who could help?" Crowbill taps two places on the desk as though marking a quay. "Two men dressed as porters. A skiff below them with an oarsman. You take the stair. Four bodies, none standing in a clump like fools." He looks up. "Enough?"

summary: Halla reluctantly takes Nus's offered hand. Nus says, 'I get us in, you get us out. How quiet can you be in that mail?'

Halla asks whether Crowbill's huge half-orc enforcer can help. Crowbill names Kag as the fighter assigned beside Halla at the water-stair, sets the other man at the alley and the oarsman below, then asks whether Halla accepts if Crowbill clears the barge.
narrative: Halla says, "Your caper. You tell me. What about that huge half-orc woman you have working for you?" Crowbill answers, "Kag. She was one of them. She holds the stair with you; the other man covers the alley, and the oarsman takes the boy. Four is enough. Five is a gathering, and gatherings get noticed." He turns the open ledger toward Halla. "If I clear the barge, are you in?"

summary: Halla accepts Crowbill's revised conditional contract. He will never board the DragonBarge; the operation proceeds only if Hanzo and Vask are ashore, with Halla and Kag covering Nus's retreat. Crowbill introduces Nus.
narrative: Halla accepts the revised shore-side job: "Yep. For once, I'd be more than happy to." Crowbill draws a line under the account. "Good. This exists only if Hanzo and Vask are ashore. My runner finds you after your bout; no runner, no job." He unbolts the inner door. A wiry young man dressed rather better than the chandlery below warrants comes through, rolling a copper coin over his knuckles. Crowbill says, "Nus. Halla holds the stair with Kag. You go alone." Nus catches the coin and offers Halla his hand. "Nus."

summary: Halla grins, calls Nus crazy for attempting the DragonBarge job, and says he almost respects him. Nus answers that almost will do and keeps his hand offered.
narrative: Halla grins at Nus and says, "You are fucking crazy to try this. I almost respect you." Nus keeps his offered hand between them; his grin widens. "Almost will do. Crowbill's never managed that much."

summary: Player-requested rewind to Crowbill's offer. Retracted acceptance event myth-event-32ceb4f804a7 and Nus introduction myth-event-1f47460351e8; superseded acceptance fact myth-fact-e28938ff2923 and removed its knowledge edges. Six-gold payment survives: Halla has1GP and owes8GP. Locket disclosure and Crowbill's unanswered guard offer survive. Halla has not met Nus.
Halla accepts Nus's offered hand. The two meet and seal their part in Crowbill's conditional shore-side extraction plan with a handshake.
narrative: Halla takes Nus's offered hand and shakes it.

summary: After Halla and Nus shake hands, Crowbill closes the ledger and repeats that his runner will find Halla after the bout only if the operation proceeds. He opens the office door.
narrative: Nus grips Halla's hand once and lets go. Crowbill closes the ledger. "Tomorrow, after your bout. No runner, no job." He opens the office door onto the chandlery stairs.

summary: Halla returns to his sister's Forge Quarter yard and spends the remaining daylight drilling quietly with battleaxe and handaxe. He finishes at dusk without interruption.
narrative: Halla leaves Crowbill's office and returns through the Forge Quarter to his sister's boat-repair yard. In the narrow strip behind the repair shed, screened by stacked timber and the canal wall, he spends the remaining daylight drilling with battleaxe and handaxe: footwork, changes of guard, short combinations and clean recoveries. Nobody interrupts him. At dusk he wipes both axes and secures them. No money, injury, Luck or fatigue changes; this is ordinary practice, not an experience improvement.

summary: OOC canon correction: retracted the invented singing-voice theft and patronage-refusal motive. Restored the source campaign's inciting event: Santo attempted to seat a lust spirit in Emmeralda using the stolen Seat the Bound scroll. The original poor-chance working treats the recorded 44 as a Hard failure; Santo fled with a burned hand after attacking her, Gardwen and Magda saved her, and the ritual evidence remained. Halla has not learned any of this.

Halla caught a Dragon Knight planting a tarred parcel beneath a repair hull in his sister yard. Halla blocked his escape, wounded him in the head and seriously disabled his left arm, then accepted his surrender. Halla carried the parcel and marched the unarmed prisoner into the house; the broadsword remained in the shed.
narrative: The Knight surrendered after Halla counterstruck his failed rush. Halla said, "Let’s get you inside bub," took the tarred parcel, and brought the prisoner into the house.

summary: Halla carefully opened the tarred parcel with Mechanisms14/47 success, preserving its wrapping and knots. Inside were silver fittings stamped with Baron Hanzo dragon mark, confirming the prisoner account and the attempted theft frame.
narrative: Halla opened the parcel slowly and without damaging the wrapping. The contents matched the captured Knight explanation.

summary: Asked why he planted the parcel, the captured Knight says a patrol sergeant ordered it because Halla kept interfering with Dragon Knight seizures. The intended watch search would close the yard and bring theft charges.
narrative: Halla asks, "Why did you want to do something like that?" The prisoner answers that he did not want it; his sergeant ordered the planting because Halla kept interfering. The watch was meant to search the yard at dawn.

summary: Halla sends his sister to Crowbill with the preserved tarred wrapping and stamped silver fittings, asking her to bring Crowbill back to question the captured Dragon Knight. Halla remains at the yard guarding the wounded prisoner.
narrative: Halla tells his sister, "My love. Can you go get one of our old friends from Crowbill? I’m thinking they might want to talk to this one. Take the package since he’s got some expertise about dealing with thieves."

summary: Halla gives Crowbill the captured Dragon Knight and planted silver, refuses further involvement with the prisoner, and asks for a safe place for himself and his sister. Crowbill accepts and offers the secured inner room behind his shuttered chandlery without interfering with Halla d1 tournament bout.
narrative: Halla says, "I don’t want anything. He’s yours as is the silver. He’ll be missed though, and he was ordered to do this so we can’t stay here. Can you find my sister and me a place to stay till the ruckus passes? I want nothing to do with this piece of garbage. And I’ve got a date on the sands tomorrow."

summary: Gardwen reached the after hold, but Orrin Fear held. Love87/70 failed against Fear20/65 success; he ordered her off the ship without betraying her or revealing the boy secret.
narrative: Gardwen told Orrin the truth. His Love for the boy rolled87/70, failure; Fear of the Baron rolled20/65, success. Fear won. He did not call the mail-clad watch, but stood in her way and told her to leave. She withdrew without reaching Cailan or learning the binding anchors.

summary: Gardwen slipped through the doubled DragonBarge watch with Hard Stealth33/34, reached Orrin below, but his Fear won and he turned her away without raising the alarm. She left without reaching Cailan or learning the anchors.
narrative: Gardwen boarded the DragonBarge unseen despite the doubled watch. Her Hard Stealth roll33 succeeded against effective34. Below, Orrin heard the truth but Fear of the Baron beat Love of the boy; he barred the way, did not call the watch, and made her leave. She withdrew unseen. The planned revelations about Thuban, the bones and the locket were not learned.

summary: Halla takes his shield, chainmail, helm, battleaxe, handaxe, dagger and tournament kit, leaving ordinary belongings and yard property behind. Crowbill men remove the prisoner and evidence; Halla and his sister enter the secured inner room behind Crowbill shuttered chandlery for the night.
narrative: Halla says, "My shield and full kit. Leave everything else." He and his sister leave the yard before the missing Knight can bring retaliation to their door.

summary: Crowbill values the captured Dragon Knight and preserved planted silver at four gold, cutting Halla's debt from eight to four. Tomorrow's conditional locket job keeps its eight-gold value: four debt clearance and four cash on success. Safe lodging remains free.

This concludes our business unless you are seeking help from the Princes Guard in the same way that we serve any citizen of Purewater'. Halla tenders the authorised four gold. Crowbill accepts, marks account paid and gives written acknowledgment before making any further request. Ward witnesses it. Crowbill: 'Paid in full. No more debt.' Then: 'Then I am asking as a citizen. Marr’s men mean to take a boat tonight. Will your Guard protect its crew?' Request for ordinary protection only, not concealed cargo passage. No information/protection supplied yet, no agenda progress. Crowbill has no remaining debt leverage; independent interests remain. Halla purse0/debt0; dagger already sold.

summary: Halla insists on lawful declaration; Crowbill agrees to redirect the cloth boat through customs.

Ownership is his claim, not independently proved. Ward said cargo must go through customs and protection does not waive duty. Player now: 'By the book. Crowbill. It needs to be by the book'. Crowbill agrees to send the boat for declaration and asks that Marr's men be kept off crew; no tax payment, declaration or ownership ruling has occurred. Ward requires boat name, master's name and expected approach so a patrol can meet and escort it to customs. Crowbill has not yet supplied identifying details or dispatched instructions; outcome pending. Halla's paid debt remains zero, no private obligation or information bargain reinstated.

Boat not confirmed arrived. Crowbill hands Halla written instructions directing master to declare six wool bales and accompany Guard to harbour customs. Master has not received them. Halla accepts carrying message; Ward accompanies. No duty paid, no ownership resolved, no clock advance.

She reads, agrees to follow patrol boat to customs and prepares to cast off; declaration and ownership settlement remain pending. Q2 preempted by player intervention; Marr receives no cloth/proceeds/clock segment. Ward orders return to guardroom after custody handover; no travel or sling issue yet. Same d6/dusk.

summary: Nimras begins at Vey’s House of Small Windows; Vey offers the sealed case Vaur left for an agent of the fellowship. Nimras has not accepted or opened it.
narrative: Dusk in the House of Small Windows on High Isle. Beeswax, warm paper and canal sounds in the front workroom. Nimras has his letter of introduction. Oren Vey, elderly in a pale grey coat with an ink-stained cuff, offers a cedar case bound with wax-sealed cord and addressed in Rennic Vaur’s hand. Vey says: “Rennic left this for whoever they sent after him. Do you want it opened here?” No response or action by Nimras has yet occurred.

summary: Nimras asks Vey to open Vaur’s case and reads his former teacher’s invitation to Lantern Float Market.
narrative: Nimras smiles to himself and thinks: “That’s just like him.” He says: “Yes. Let’s see what he has to say.” Vey cuts the waxed cord and lifts the lid. Inside, a brass-mounted lens lies cracked across its centre, beside a folded landing sketch and a note in Rennic’s hand: “Before you call this theft, look at what they are closing. Lantern Float Market. Ask for Rennic.” The sketch labels a public landing at the market. Vey places the note within Nimras’s reach. Nimras has not yet selected his next action or taken the case.

summary: Nimras visually examines the cracked lens and asks Vey to retain it; Vey agrees.
narrative: Nimras says: “Very well. Thank you Vey.” He examines the lens under the lamplight. The fracture splits the view; the brass focusing collar turns. Routine visual examination reveals no further useful feature; no magical inspection is made. Following his conditional instruction, Nimras asks: “Would you hold onto this?” Vey replies: “Of course.” Vey settles the lens into its cedar case and sets it on a shelf behind his desk. The note and landing sketch remain on the table. Nimras has not departed.

summary: Nimras follows the sketch to Lantern Float Market and asks for Rennic, finding him taking soundings beside a repair bench.
narrative: Nimras takes Rennic’s note and landing sketch and follows footbridges and waterside paths from High Isle to Lantern Float Market. One watch passes, d6/dusk to d6/night. The cracked lens remains with Vey. Ordinary directions lead to Rennic’s rented repair bench. Frying fish, lamp oil and rope creak surround the pontoons. Rennic kneels at the edge with a sounding line running through his hands. A leather manuscript case rests beneath the bench. Rennic grins when he sees Nimras and offers him the wooden reel: “Nimras. Take the reel a moment, would you?” Nimras has not answered or accepted it, and no arrest, bargain or surrender has occurred.

summary: Nimras takes Rennic’s sounding reel and remarks that his teacher does not seem worried. Rennic asks what the fellowship told him.
narrative: Nimras says: “Master Rennic. You don’t seem too worried by my being here.” He takes the reel. The cord is wet and gritty, drawn taut by the sounding weight. Rennic checks the marked length against the pontoon edge and records the depth on a slate. He says: “I hoped they’d send someone who knew me. What have they told you?” The manuscript case remains beneath the bench; no recovery or contract disclosure has occurred. The ordinary handover and measurement have no meaningful uncertainty and no roll is made.

summary: Nimras states the accusation and return instruction; Rennic admits retaining a loaned survey and opens the case.
narrative: Nimras says: “Only that you took something you shouldn’t have. And that you’re to come back with me.” Rennic sets his slate beside the bench and brings up the leather case. He says: “I kept a survey they’d lent me. It’s here.” He opens it and unfolds an old sheet, its blue-marked water route crossed by fresh pencil annotations matching the current waterfront. COMMON INTAKE is written beside the route. Nimras still holds the reel; no manuscript handover or agreement to return has occurred.

summary: Nimras examines the survey and can follow its labelled intake, maintenance passage and market overlay.
narrative: Nimras looks at the survey and asks whether he understands it. The labelled layout is readable to a literate trained scholar: blue line freshwater intake, narrow parallel maintenance passage, fresh pencil outline of market pontoons above their route, circled access stair on the southern bank. This establishes what the map claims, not its accuracy or present legal force. No skill check is made for ordinary legible map-reading. Rennic retains the survey; Nimras still has the sounding reel. No time advance.

summary: Asked for a plain explanation, Rennic describes his concern about shared waterworks access and asks Nimras to inspect the entrance.
narrative: Nimras asks what Rennic meant by looking at what they are closing, what the common intake issue is, and why Rennic came knowing someone would pursue him; he calls him old friend and says he is not making sense. Rennic secures the sounding line to a cleat, freeing Nimras’s hands, and flattens the survey on the bench. He says: “The intake supplied fresh water to the waterfront. The passage beside it gave access for repairs. I’ve heard quay leases are being bought up; if those entrances are included, the new owners could shut everyone else out. I haven’t proved that yet.” He continues: “I needed the original’s measurements here, against the actual channel. I should have returned it when asked, and I knew they’d send someone. I want to finish the comparison before going home. Will you help me check the entrance?” No acceptance, departure, manuscript transfer or new watch occurs. The fuller answer follows the player’s explicit request for clarification of the previously unclear account.

summary: Nimras agrees to the inspection; he and Rennic reach the southern intake stair, where lower steps are submerged.
narrative: Nimras says “Sure”, smiles and shakes his head, privately reflecting that this is typical of Rennic’s pursuit of a potential injustice. Rennic rolls the survey, shoulders the manuscript case and brings his work lamp. A short walk over the market walkways brings them to the southern-bank stone stair within the same night watch. Damp stone and water sounds replace the frying-fish smell. An old bronze plate labels the intake. Lower treads disappear beneath dark water, while a narrow ledge is visible beyond the low arch, just above the surface. No new lock or guard is present. Neither character has attempted the submerged steps or passage. Nimras’s next approach is undecided.

summary: Nimras’s cautious Perception check succeeds: 14 against70. He spots the broken tread corner before entry.
narrative: Nimras asks “Are we expecting trouble?” and directs a cautious approach. Rennic says: “Wet stone and deep water. I haven’t seen anyone guarding it.” Nimras inspects from the dry steps before entering. Perception, Standard70; official CLI roll14, success, critical range7. He sees a broken outer corner on the first submerged tread, intact inner stone and floating scraps drawing inward beneath the arch. No automatic fall, movement, damage or entry is resolved. Rennic has not been told the check’s findings merely by being nearby.

summary: Nimras keeps Invisibility prepared without casting and watches Rennic while they enter by the known intact footing. They find chalk marks at an old intake grille.
narrative: Nimras agrees to continue, asks to have Invisibility ready if he needs to disappear, and privately directs attention to Rennic because he does not fully trust him. Invisibility was already prepared and remains uncast: no magic points spent, no held combat action or automatic reaction created. They use the exposed intact inner steps beside the wall, avoiding the previously spotted break; water reaches their boot tops. Slow ordinary movement over this now-known sound route needs no repeat check. Rennic goes only a few paces ahead with lamp and manuscript case visible. Beyond the bend is a dry service recess beside an old grated intake mouth. Fresh white chalk rectangles mark the worn stone jambs. Rennic stops beside them with the manuscript under his arm. Nimras has not inspected the marks closely or cast a spell. No attack, gate installation or watch advance occurs.

summary: Nimras watches as Rennic checks the chalk and leads towards a measuring crew in the adjoining bay.
narrative: Nimras directs: “Watch him. Let him take the lead.” Rennic checks the chalk rectangle against the folded survey, then follows the ledge towards a scrape and another pool of lamplight. A broad-shouldered woman in a wool work jacket holds a folding rule against the stone; an adult assistant waits beside a canvas toolbag and a paper on a board. Rennic walks towards them, manuscript case still under his arm. Nimras remains at the bend with Rennic and the work bay in view. No conversation, attack, spell or concealment attempt has occurred. The crew’s names and affiliation have not been introduced to Nimras. Same night watch.

summary: Nimras joins Rennic in the work light. The fitter asks whether they are from Marr’s and describes the proposed lockable gate.
narrative: Nimras agrees to join Rennic and steps into the work lamp’s light. The fitter folds her rule and sets it beside the clipped paper, whose heading reads MARR FREIGHT. She says to Nimras: “Are you from Marr’s? Their order says a lockable gate across this opening.” Rennic stands beside Nimras with the manuscript case. The assistant remains by the tools. No introduction, answer by Nimras, deception, agreement, attack or spell has occurred. The order is for an estimate, not proof of ownership or a completed installation.

summary: At Nimras’s pause Rennic answers truthfully; the fitter explains she is estimating and offers the order.
narrative: Nimras waits for Rennic to answer. Rennic lays the survey beside the fitter’s board and says: “No. I’m comparing the old survey with what’s still here.” The fitter sets her rule aside and turns the clipped order towards Nimras: “I’ve only been asked for an estimate. The order’s there if you want to look.” Neither mage has examined the order in detail. No gate installation, dispute resolution, identity deception or watch advance occurs.

A dog-sized creature of clear glass follows him, blue light burning inside its throat. Rennic spots you. “Nimras! Mind the thing behind me!”

summary: Nimras arrives for the first time at West Lantern Landing, with a fellowship introduction to Oren Vey and public directions toward High Isle. He has not yet approached a contact.
narrative: Purewater, after nightfall. The ferry nudges West Lantern Landing beneath a clatter of mooring chains. Beyond the quay, bridges climb between crowded houses and lanterns tremble on black canal water. Your fellowship’s introduction is addressed to Oren Vey, House of Small Windows, High Isle. Under the landing’s awning, a public route-board marks High Isle and its crossings. You have a contact’s address, your staff, and a city you have never visited.

summary: Nimras follows public directions to the House of Small Windows on High Isle and encounters Oren Vey at the open front window. He has not yet introduced himself or shown the fellowship letter.
narrative: Following the marked footbridges, you reach High Isle without trouble. The House of Small Windows stands beside a narrow canal, lamplight behind its shutters. Through an open window, an elderly man in a grey coat looks up from a table crowded with books. “Oren Vey,” he says. “Come to the door; I can hear you better there.”

summary: Nimras Lylandyr introduces himself and his search for Rennic. Vey welcomes him and supplies the old Three Steps Rooms address and retained note.
narrative:
Player: “Master Vey. I’m Nimras Lylandyr; sent by my commission to search for a mage called Rennic. I believe you are expecting me”

Vey opens the door and clears a folded letter from beneath a book, laying it on the corner of his worktable. “Yes; come in, Master Lylandyr. Rennic left me an address—Three Steps Rooms, in the Merchant Quarter—and I’ve kept his note.”

summary: Nimras asks directions and reads Rennic’s lodging note. Vey gives the canal route and Elna Pike contact.
narrative:
Player: “Thank you sir: could you give me directions? I’m new in town. Read the note”

Vey says: “Cross back to the Merchant Quarter and follow the canal east; look for a green lamp above three stone steps. Ask for Elna Pike.”

The note is in Rennic’s familiar handwriting and reads:
Vey—

I’m lodging at Three Steps Rooms. Leave word with Elna Pike if I’m out. I have a binding problem to pick apart. For once, it isn’t one of my own making.

Rennic

summary: Nimras carefully approaches Three Steps Rooms. Perception70/70 success beats Bess Stealth86/45 failure; he spots the lookout while Iven asks Elna for access and is refused the key. No entry or attack resolved.
narrative:
Player: “I’ll try to navigate down there immediately. Keep my eyes open and be fairly careful the whole way there.”

Actual CLI roll-opposed: Nimras Perception70/70 success; Bess Stealth86/45 failure; winner Nimras.

The green lamp comes into view across a short footbridge. A thickset man stands on the lodging’s steps, one hand braced against the door. Across the canal, a woman waits beneath an awning, a cudgel tucked against her leg; her attention keeps returning to that doorway. “You can leave a message for Master Vaur,” a woman says from inside. “You can’t have his key.”

summary: Nimras questions the lookout about her cudgel. Bess acknowledges a joint collection job for an unnamed employer and threatens obstruction; Iven looks towards Nimras. No names, commission or employer revealed.
narrative:
Player: “What’s going on madam? Why the cudgel?”

The woman steps out from beneath the awning, the cudgel loose in her hand. She nods towards the man on the steps. “Collecting something for our employer. The stick’s for people who make that difficult.” The man turns to look at you.

summary: Nimras takes a friendly tone and offers help. Bess names Rennic Vaur as the quarry and asks whether Nimras knows him. No identity, employer or allegiance disclosed by Nimras.
narrative:
Player direction: Keep it very friendly.
Player speech: “I know, people can be unhelpful and unfriendly. Who are you looking for, maybe I can help.”

She rests the cudgel against her boot, keeping hold of the handle. “Rennic Vaur—a travelling magician with a leather satchel. You know him?”

No roll required for Bess voluntarily naming the person she is seeking; she has not been persuaded to reveal confidential control or employer details.

summary: Nimras asks why the two seek Rennic. Bess says their employer wants his satchel and Rennic brought with it, referring further questions to the unnamed female employer.
narrative:
Player: “That’s interesting. Why are you looking for him?”

“Our employer wants the satchel he’s carrying, and him with it. Beyond that, you’d have to ask her.”

Bess states her actual assignment, without claiming ownership, a warrant or knowledge of the manuscript. No persuasion or deception resolution is required for that voluntary answer.

summary: Nimras admits he is also looking for Rennic and asks to meet the employer. Bess names Captain Senn at the Drowned Kiln, offers an escort and asks his name. No departure or report yet.
narrative:
Player: “I’m looking for him too. Could I meet your employer”

The woman lifts the cudgel from her boot and tucks it beneath her coat. “Captain Senn, down at the Drowned Kiln; I can take you. What name shall I give her?”

Bess has an ordinary practical route to her employer and offers a potentially useful professional contact without assuming alliance or promising Senn’s agreement. She knows only Nimras’s stated interest. No lie, covert Insight success or allegiance is inferred.

summary: Nimras gives the cover name Damien Harcourt. Bess uses it provisionally, introduces herself, and crosses to coordinate the offered escort with Iven. Escort agreement and departure not yet resolved.
narrative:
Player: “Damien Harcourt.”

“Bess,” she says. “Wait here, Harcourt; I’ll tell my mate where I’m going.” She crosses towards the lodging steps.

No name challenge, identity inspection or automatic lie detection occurred. Iven remains at the room-search position; Senn has not been informed.

summary: Bess briefly coordinates with her companion, leaves Iven at the lodging, and returns to the footbridge ready to lead Harcourt to Captain Senn.
narrative: Bess has a quick word with the man on the steps, then returns to the bridge. “This way, Harcourt.” Iven stays at the lodging; Nimras has not yet followed.

narrative: Actual engine roll: Iven Deceit52/35failure versus Elna Insight1/65critical; winner Elna. She catches the false prior-permission claim and bars the common-room entrance before Iven can press inside. He remains outside, without a room key or receipt lead. No injury, alert to Captain Senn or knowledge of the loft follows automatically. Nimras and Bess are absent and do not learn this.

Player Luck instruction: “Luck - switch the roll”

Captain Senn, cropped-haired and wearing a neatly patched coat, turns from a moored lighter as Bess introduces Harcourt. “Harcourt, is it? What’s your business with Vaur?”

narrative: Original failed conversation is superseded by the requested permitted digit reversal. New disclosure delivered to Nimras and held by Bess, not automatically reported to Senn. No time rewind or resource refresh. Audit of original dice preserved.

summary: Nimras examines the glass hound. Arcane Knowledge2/70critical recognises ongoing animation, exposed silver bridge vulnerability and separate removable trace receptacle. No spell cast.
narrative:
Player: “Take a look at the glass hound. Have I seen anything like that before?”

Actual CLI roll-skill Arcane Knowledge2/70critical. Critical recognises visible binding architecture through transparent body and distinguishes animation from the separate trace module. Grants no maker identity, exact stored casting value, all command words, buyer knowledge or automated success on a future intervention.

The principles are familiar from your training in constructed guardians, though this particular design is new. Through its clear chest you can see silver threads joined by a narrow bridge: a vulnerable part of the animation binding. The blue throat-piece is a separate, removable receptacle for a magical trace—something the hound could use to follow a particular caster. The animation could be unravelled with your own magic.

summary: Harcourt says Vaur took something belonging to someone else and withholds details. Nimras assesses Senn as a mercenary captain from visible gear and command role; Senn states living recovery and satchel objectives.
narrative:
Player speech: “He took something that didn’t belong to him. Can’t really say much more.”
Player asks: “Take a look at Senn any sense of his profession?”

Her equipment and the crew’s deference suggest an experienced mercenary captain: patched padded coat, well-kept shortsword, practical boots. A brass whistle hangs at her belt.

Senn: “I need him alive, and I need his satchel. Does that clash with your instructions?”

No roll needed for a broad impression from obvious weapons, coat and command role. No inference of secret motives, exact class, magical capability, client or legal powers. The stated theft is consistent with actual fellowship ownership, but Senn does not know that ownership or the visitor’s client.

summary: Harcourt conditionally offers cooperation if he can take Vaur afterwards, smiling and presenting as reasonable and unthreatening. Senn counteroffers a handover on d8/afternoon while retaining the satchel. Acceptance pending.
narrative:
Player speech: “Not necessarily. As long as I can take him when you’re done with him”
Player follow-up: “Smile- I’m very reasonable. Don’t look particularly dangerous either”

Nimras smiles and maintains an outwardly amiable, unthreatening manner; no additional PC dialogue, motives or thoughts invented.

Senn smiles back. “I need him until the afternoon after next. You can take him afterwards, but his satchel stays with me.”

This is a voluntary counteroffer aligned with Senn’s planned d8 demonstration and retention of the manuscript, not automatic persuasion, a completed agreement or an assured handover. Senn does not learn Nimras’s magic, true identity or actual danger from the smile. No reveal of buyer or intended demonstration. No extra action or roll occurred during the interrupted preparation turn.

summary: Harcourt verbally accepts Senn’s handover-and-satchel terms and points to the hound. Senn signals its attention with her whistle and describes tracking from a fresh magical trace.
narrative:
Player: “That’s fine… what is THAT? Pointing at the glass hound”

Senn nods, then sounds a short note on her brass whistle. The glass head swivels towards her. “A tracker; give it a fresh trace of a magician’s work, and it follows the trail. Saves a great deal of asking at doors.”

Verbal terms: Senn to have Vaur until d8 afternoon after her business, then Harcourt may take him; Senn retains satchel. No magical oath, transfer, capture or guarantee of future success. PC’s private motives and future choices remain his. The whistle draws attention; HoundII remains held, with no loaded sample, attack or tracking action. Senn gives a truthful high-level description without explaining buyer or intended demonstration.

summary: At Harcourt’s request Senn demonstrates HoundII returning and holding on whistle commands. She asks for a fresh magical trace for a tracking demonstration; none supplied or loaded yet.
narrative:
Player: “Huh. Now that is pretty cool. Can you run it?”

Senn walks to the far side of the yard and blows her whistle. The hound springs after her, glass feet clattering over stone; another note brings it to a dead stop. “Movement’s easy. For tracking, I need a fresh magical trace—have you got one?”

Senn moves within the dry18x12m yard, remaining within30m command range. Trained return and hold commands face no opposition, hazard or uncertainty, so require no roll. HoundII remains physically intact, with no loaded trace. The demonstration neither identifies Harcourt as a caster nor supplies a trace by assumption. No third-party hunt, spell, capture or attack occurs.

summary: Harcourt laughs off supplying a trace and offers field help and information. Senn names glassworker Doria Flint at Furnace Court as a contact to question about Vaur, and asks for word if found.
narrative:
Player: “That’s ok. Laugh. Anything I can do? I’m new in town but I’d be happy to share information if I find his trail.”

Nimras laughs and provides no trace or spell.

narrative: At d7/dawn Nimras stayed beside Conall guarding the surrendered company. Roughly forty minutes passed without another attack or escape. Kest delivered Conall request at High Isle Watch post and returned with Sergeant Abel Weir and the receiving duty officer. Conall showed his warrant and Varro letter and gave his eyewitness account of the inspection, conflicting hound commands, lightning strike, Bess attack and company surrender. summary: Nimras gives Weir his commission, cover and full fight account; Conall offers to finish Kiln handover
narrative: Nimras identified himself to Weir as Nimras Lylanddyr (the established character Nimras Lylandyr), a freelance mage hunter commissioned by his former independent fellowship to find his old mentor Rennic Vaur alive and recover its entrusted manuscript. In his full explanation he described using Damien Harcourt as cover, posing as an interested buyer to infiltrate Senn company, the conditional arrangement to receive Rennic after Senn business, and his subsequent discovery of the mage-hunting conversion. He explained finding Rennic, their decision to report to the Assay, the report through Holt, and Conall joining the inspection under buyer cover. He recounted the demonstration, Conall revealing his warrant, the letter and whistles recovered from the chest, Senn ordering Iven to recall the hounds, Nimras warning Iven and then striking him and the two hounds with lightning when he used the whistle, Bess cudgel attack, his staff parry and disarm, Conall intervention, Senn surrender, checking Iven and summoning the Watch. He did not claim a prior hound attack or existing state warrant of his own. His narrative authorizes this summary, not invented verbatim PC dialogue or an undisclosed fellowship name. No hidden refuge address, manuscript surrender, buyer private whereabouts or immunity is supplied. Weir took Nimras account and retained it alongside Conall eyewitness account and the Varro letter evidence. He did not detain Nimras or pronounce guilt, innocence or immunity; Watch custody of the surrendered company and guarding of the Kiln continued. Conall told Nimras, "I can finish here. Rennic is still on Temple Isle." This offers to handle the remaining Kiln procedure without obliging Nimras to fetch officials or stay; Nimras has not yet left or chosen his next destination. The chest key remains temporarily with Nimras, the four whistles and letter with Conall, and the chest contents unchanged.

summary: Hrill coldly refuses Garr’s hunting offer; Garr states commercial motive and asks Grey Heron to keep clear of hunting lines.
narrative: At White Shingle, aboard Grey Heron alongside the jetty, Hrill declines Garr Hew’s six-gold hunting offer in an explicitly frosty tone: “I have no stomach for it. I’ll fight any man with a blade in his hand but never some poor beast for sport. Good day to you.” Garr lowers his greeting hand; his grin disappears. He answers: “There’s a buyer for that shell. Keep clear of our lines, and we’ll keep clear of you.” He turns back to the harpoon on its trestles and checks the line at its head. No contract, payment, weapon drawn, attack or departure occurs. The channel beside Grey Heron remains open.

Ilyen calls, “I’m Ilyen; keep your steel sheathed, and there’s no hunting inside this inlet. What brings you north?” No answer, agreement or attack yet. All crew and cargo intact.
